analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Enterprises is a sprawling conglomerate (steel trading, real estate, mining, engineering, and pizza outlets) built atop a near-dormant shell with revenue of just ₹1 Cr in 2020–21, now priced at 78x EV/EBITDA with ROCE of only 5.97% — far below any reasonable cost of capital. Reported profits are largely manufactured by "Other Income" (₹83–159 Cr annually), not by the operating business, making the earnings quality deeply suspect.
key_strengths: Revenue trajectory is real: ₹1 Cr (2021) → ₹1,488 Cr (2025), demonstrating some operational build-out
Low financial leverage at Debt/Equity 0.16 (though borrowings jumped 5x to ₹671 Cr in FY25)
Promoter holding of 62.72% aligns management with long-term outcomes
key_risks: Earnings quality is fraudulent-adjacent: Other Income (₹159 Cr in FY22, ₹135 Cr in FY24, ₹83 Cr in FY25) routinely exceeds or matches operating profit — reported net profits are not from the business
Egregious valuation: EV/EBITDA of 78x and P/E of 37x for a steel trader with 6% operating margins and ROCE of 5.97%
Conglomerate sprawl (steel, real estate, mining, gold, pizza) with no identifiable moat — classic value-destroying diversification into unrelated businesses
red_flags: Shell company transformation: revenue was ₹1 Cr in FY20-21, name changed from 'Shree Global Tradefin' in Sept 2023 — classic reverse-merger/shell game pattern
Reserves exploded from ₹198 Cr (2020) to ₹3,170 Cr (2025) — 16x growth implies massive equity dilution via QIPs; shareholders have been repeatedly diluted
FCF/Net Income = 62% (FY25) — below 80% quality threshold; OCF positive only 3 of 5 years
Near-zero institutional ownership: FII 0.69%, DII 0.07% — sophisticated capital wants nothing to do with this
Operating CF was negative in FY22 and FY24 despite reported profits — cash is not following earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Lloyds Enterprises fails every quality test I apply. ROCE at 5.97% and ROE at 2.48% mean this business destroys value relative to its cost of capital — paying 78x EV/EBITDA for that privilege is financial masochism. The operating margin of 6% on steel trading provides no cushion, and the EBITDA of ₹184 Cr in FY25 is dwarfed by a market cap of ₹9,684 Cr. Worse, reported net profits of ₹123–175 Cr in recent years are largely illusory: stripping out "Other Income" (financial investment gains, asset sales), the business earns a fraction of that. In FY22, Other Income of ₹159 Cr exceeded total revenue of ₹48 Cr — this is not an operating company, it is a financial holding vehicle dressed up as one.

The provenance of this company should disqualify it immediately. Revenue of ₹1 Cr for two consecutive years (2020–21), a name change in 2023, and reserves that grew 16x in five years via equity issuances signal a shell company that has been repeatedly used to raise capital from the public. Running pizza outlets alongside iron mining and steel trading is not diversification — it is chaos, and history shows conglomerates of this type reliably destroy capital. With institutional investors holding a combined 0.76%, the smart money has already passed judgment. This is a trading vehicle for retail speculation, not an investment.
